LESSON: THEATRE ADJUDICATION

Grade: Grade 10
Subject: THEATRE AND FILM
Strand: Theatre, Film and Society
Topic 3.1: Theatre Adjudication
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Theatre Adjudication, part of Theatre, Film and Society in Grade 10 THEATRE AND FILM.

Key inquiry question: How important is adjudication to the theatre production process? 2. Why is it important to have a criteria when adjudicating a stage performance?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. research on the criteria for adjudicating stage (play and poetry) performances (script, theme, use of voice and body, movement, lighting, sound, costume, make-up, stage set, creativity, originality, improvisation, overall impression),

2. develop a criteria for adjudicating a play,

3. develop a criteria for adjudicating a spoken word,

4. adjudicate stage plays using the set-out criteria,

5. adjudicate poetry using the set-out criteria,

6. write an adjudication report and present it orally to peers for experience sharing, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. research on the criteria for adjudicating stage (play and poetry) performances (script, theme, use of voice and body, movement, lighting, sound, costume, make-up, stage set, creativity, originality, improvisation, overall impression),
2. develop a criteria for adjudicating a play,
3. develop a criteria for adjudicating a spoken word,
4. adjudicate stage plays using the set-out criteria,
5. adjudicate poetry using the set-out criteria,
6. write an adjudication report and present it orally to peers for experience sharing, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Theatre Adjudication together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: the learner develops reflective skills while evaluating productions.

● Self-efficacy: the learner develops self-confidence during analysis of theatre.

● Communication: the learner acquires negotiation, speaking and presentation skills while presenting the adjudication report.

Values:
● Respect: the learner develops communication etiquette while critiquing performances.

● Responsibility: the learner develops a sense of obligation toward group effort when evaluating theatre productions.

● Integrity: the learner appreciates the value of truthful feedback to peers during evaluation.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Life Skills: the learner acquires assertiveness during group presentations and peer evaluation.

● Peer Education and Mentorship: the learner works with peers and mentors whilst evaluating productions.
